7615606.extract:
A New Old Play is a 2021 Chinese film directed by Qiu Jiongjiong that explores the life and career of Qiu Fu, a renowned clown in Sichuan opera. The film chronicles Qiu Fu's life from the 1920s to the 1980s through his remembrances during his journey into the netherworld. The play delves into the birth of the New-New Theatre and Opera School in Sichuan Province, depicting the impact of civil war and political changes on the development of Sichuan opera.

In the film, Qiu Fu, the topmost clown-actor of the 20th century Sichuan opera, passes away in an accident in 1980. Half-unwillingly, he sets off for the Ghost City, where he recounts his vivid memories of his life, including his childhood, performances, family tragedies, and the political events he experienced. The film intertwines personal and national history, presenting a vaudevillian theater of China's many pivots.

The film stars Yi Sicheng as Qiu Fu, a renowned Sichuan opera actor of the New-New Theatre School. Guan Nan portrays Tong Huafeng, Qiu's wife, and Qiu Zhimin plays Pocky, a military doctor. Other notable actors include Haoyu Chen, Guan Nan, Tang Hao, Xue Xuchun, Tao Gu, and Xu Gang.

The film was produced by Icarus Films and directed by Qiu Jiongjiong. It premiered at the First Look Festival in North America in March 2022, making its debut in the film industry. The production of the film was a significant event in the Chinese film industry, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of Sichuan opera.

Critical reception of the film has been generally positive. Some reviewers praised its unique storytelling and the way it intertwined personal and national history. The film has received awards and nominations, highlighting its cultural significance. However, others have noted its lengthy runtime and complex narrative structure, which may be challenging for some viewers.

Qiu Fu, the most renowned clown of Sichuan opera, has reached the netherworld. Welcomed by Ox-Head and Horse-Face, shepherds of the dead, he recounts his life with the “New-New” opera troupe before his turn at the Bridge of Forgetfulness. Starting in the 1920s, Qiu’s tale melds with China’s tumultuous century into the Second Sino-Japanese War, the Great Leap Forward, and other socio-political revolutions.

Inspired by his own grandfather’s life, Qiu Jiongjiong’s A New Old Play is a sumptuous intermingling of personal and national history. It transforms China’s many pivots into a vaudevillian theater of its own, culminating in a spiritual rumination on the passage of time and the role of the artist forced to weather the storm of history. Drawing from his background as a visual artist, Qiu arrives at a masterful, painterly style: flowing tableaux, carefully art-directed sets and ingenious hand-made miniatures bringing the act of remembrance into a delightful, phantasmagorical realm.

_**A New Old Play**_ (Chinese: 椒麻堂會) is a 2021 [epic film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_film "Epic film") directed and written by [Qiu Jiongjiong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qiu_Jiongjiong "Qiu Jiongjiong"). As Qiu's seventh film, it marks his first [fictional feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrative_film "Narrative film"). A co-production between Hong Kong's Uluka Productions and France's Hippocampe Productions, the film stars Yi Sicheng as Qiu Fu, a recently deceased [Sichuan opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan_opera "Sichuan opera") actor, alongside Guan Nan, Qiu Zhimin, Gu Tao, and Xue Xuchun. The story chronicles Qiu Fu's life and career in [China from the 1920s to the 1980s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_China#Modern_China "History of China") through his remembrances during his journey into the [netherworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youdu "Youdu"), featuring events such as the [Second Sino-Japanese War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War"), the [Chinese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War "Chinese Civil War"), the [Great Chinese Famine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Chinese_Famine "Great Chinese Famine"), and the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution").

Qiu Jiongjiong conceived of the project in 2017 after illustrating the [biography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biography "Biography") for his grandfather and Sichuan opera actor Qiu Fu. Inspired to tell the story with film, Qiu based the protagonist on his grandfather and began developing a screenplay from May 2017 to February 2018 under the [working title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_title "Working title")_The Neo-New Adventures_. Production design spanned six months before [principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began in August 2019 in [Leshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leshan "Leshan"), [Sichuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan "Sichuan") over three months. Post-production took place in France, with French filmmaker[Marie-Pierre Duhamel-Muller](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marie-Pierre_Duhamel-Muller&action=edit&redlink=1 "Marie-Pierre Duhamel-Muller (page does not exist)")([fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie-Pierre_Duhamel-Muller "fr:Marie-Pierre Duhamel-Muller"))involved in the editing. The film also marks the second film to be primarily in [Sichuanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuanese_dialects "Sichuanese dialects"), after the 1962 film _Conscription_.

_A New Old Play_ had its world premiere in competition for the [Golden Leopard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Leopard "Golden Leopard") at the [74th Locarno Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/74th_Locarno_Film_Festival "74th Locarno Film Festival") on 13 August 2021, where it received the [Special Jury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Jury_Prize_(Locarno_International_Film_Festival) "Special Jury Prize (Locarno International Film Festival)"). It also garnered various accolades and received positive reviews from critics, with praises particularly on its themes, narrative style and complexities, and production design. Due to [censorship in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_censorship_in_China "Film censorship in China"), only single-time private screenings were held worldwide from 2021 to 2022. The film received its first [wide release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_release "Wide release") in France on 30 April 2025.

Qiu Fu, a renowned [Sichuan opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan_opera "Sichuan opera") actor, meets his demise. [Ox-Head and Horse-Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ox-Head_and_Horse-Face "Ox-Head and Horse-Face") are sent to escort him into the [netherworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youdu "Youdu") to perform for [Yanluo Wang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yanluo_Wang "Yanluo Wang"). Qiu refuses to accept his fate and tries to flee, much to the envoys' confusion as they ask him how he, who has been an artiste since the age of eight, does not embrace death. Qiu retorts that he began his opera journey at seven and starts to reminisce about his life.

During the [Warlord Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warlord_Era "Warlord Era"), an operaphile Pocky rises through the ranks to become a military commander. He uses his newfound power to form an opera troupe called the New-New Theatre School. Early in its operation, Qiu Fu, a foundling of a famous opera actor who died performing on stage, is sent to the troupe by his mother, who abandons him to remarry. Qiu learns opera singing from the troupe's teachers, but his performances are unsatisfactory. One day, while practising, he encounters Pocky, who takes a liking to him and accepts him as an apprentice. After some training, Qiu debuts as an opera performer. The [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War") soon breaks out, and the troupe begins charity tours to raise funds against [Japan's invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War"). One night, Qiu is intoxicated after drinking a bowl of poisonous mushroom soup and dreams of flying across the city on a leaf, only to be bombed by a Japanese fighter jet.

In the netherworld, Qiu follows the envoys to the [Naihe Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-existence#Chinese_mythology "Pre-existence"), where he encounters Crooky, a servant of the troupe who mysteriously disappeared decades ago. The envoys explain that they never received orders to take Crooky, but he keeps returning to the netherworld, trapping his soul between realms. He opens an inn at the Naihe Bridge to welcome both the deceased and [demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaoguai "Yaoguai"). Qiu decides to reunite with Crooky and stays at the inn while watching his young apprentices perform [rituals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_funeral_rituals "Chinese funeral rituals") in the living world. Dissatisfied with their performances, he reminisces about his own early career.

By 1945, Qiu has established himself as an opera actor. However, Pocky, now a [warlord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warlord "Warlord"), worries about his fate under [Chiang Kai-shek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Kai-shek "Chiang Kai-shek")'s rule and loses interest in opera. Before [the Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War#Immediate_post-war_clashes_(1945%E2%80%931946) "Chinese Civil War"), he disbands the troupe to protect the actors and their families from his impending downfall. Unemployed, Qiu's life worsens even after the establishment of the [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China"), when the troupe is reformed and renamed the People's Sichuan Opera Troupe. Qiu's daughter dies subsequently during the [Great Chinese Famine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Chinese_Famine "Great Chinese Famine"), but his son Hei survives. One day, Qiu finds [an abandoned infant girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female_infanticide_in_China "Female infanticide in China") on the street and, despite his meager living conditions, takes her in. He and his wife struggle to feed her and resort to stealing [feces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_feces "Human feces"), only to be caught by [cadres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadre_system_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "Cadre system of the Chinese Communist Party") who accuse them of stealing [state property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_property "Public property"). Qiu sings to the cadres, leveraging his fame as an actor to escape. They manage to cook the [maggots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maggots "Maggots") found in the feces to feed the girl, sustaining her life. Later, the girl's mother returns, claiming she abandoned her only because her husband tried to eat the child. Though reluctant, Qiu's wife returns the baby. During the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution"), the New-New troupe is [labeled as feudal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution#Opera_and_music "Cultural Revolution"), [facing persecution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Struggle_session "Struggle session") from the [Red Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Guards "Red Guards"). Hei, now a teenager, wishes to join the [Big Link-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Exchange_of_Revolutionary_Experience "Great Exchange of Revolutionary Experience") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing") but is locked up by his family. Desperate, he escapes through a window and flies across the city on a leaf. Years later, now a high-ranking Red Guard, Hei returns home and learns that Qiu is released from [labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re-education_through_labor "Re-education through labor") and assigned to minor roles in plays.

After reminiscing about his career, Qiu bids farewell to Crooky and shares one last drink with the envoys. Confused about how he will remember all his lines after drinking the [Meng-po soup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meng_Po "Meng Po"), he is reassured by the envoys that his artistic intuition will guide him. Qiu boards the boat and reaches the other side, queuing for the Meng-po soup before drinking it all. The [camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movie_camera "Movie camera") pans to each of the other characters drinking the soup at various moments, then returns to Qiu's empty seat. [The director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qiu_Jiongjiong "Qiu Jiongjiong"), in modern attire, sits down and is served a bowl of Meng-po soup.

There is nothing new under the sun, as we know. However, these characters are just like you and me, and we each in our own way will continue to repeat this same song of humanity."

—Qiu Jiongjiong, the director and writer, on the inspiration behind the screenplay for _A New Old Play_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)

Qiu Fu, the grandfather of director [Qiu Jiongjiong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qiu_Jiongjiong "Qiu Jiongjiong"), was a [Sichuan opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan_opera "Sichuan opera") actor who gained fame for playing [_chou_ roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chou_role "Chou role")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-10) in the 1930s and 1940s throughout [Sichuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan "Sichuan").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) He died in 1987 when Qiu Jiongjiong was ten years old.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 293  Growing up in [Leshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leshan "Leshan"), Sichuan, Qiu Jiongjiong developed an interest in Sichuan opera influenced by his grandfather, which ultimately inspired him to pursue a career in filmmaking.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) He also described having a "close" relationship with his grandfather, who served as a "crucial figure in [his] artistic inspirations" for his artworks and films.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) After making the documentary film _[Mr. Zhang Believes](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mr.\_Zhang\_Believes&action=edit&redlink=1 "Mr. Zhang Believes (page does not exist)")([zh](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%99%A1\_(2014%E5%B9%B4%E7%B4%80%E9%8C%84%E7%89%87) "zh:癡 (2014年紀錄片)"))_ (2015), Qiu struggled with inspiration for several years despite still wanting to create films.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) In 2017, on the 30th anniversary of Qiu Fu's death, Qiu Jiongjiong's father began writing a [biography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biography "Biography") to commemorate Qiu Fu and asked Qiu to illustrate for the book.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia009-11) After creating illustrations for all 15 chapters in two months, Qiu felt a sense of "incompleteness" and wanted to approach the subject of his grandfather "through the medium of film", which inspired him to start writing the screenplay that would become _A New Old Play_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia009-11) It marks the second film produced by Qiu Jiongjiong featuring Qiu Fu, following the documentary short film _Ode to Joy_ (2007), which depicted a stage performance in remembrance of the 20th anniversary of Qiu Fu's death and was cited by Qiu as a significant inspiration for _A New Old Play_'s focus on the lives of ordinary people.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6)

Qiu Jiongjiong began writing the screenplay in May 2017 and completed it in February 2018, taking about seven months to finish a script that exceeded 100,000 words.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 293  He based the story on his father's biography, along with some additional background research.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) It marks Qiu's seventh film and first [fictional feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrative_film "Narrative film").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CNAJune2022-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-13) Qiu described the story itself as "[non-fictional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fictional "Non-fictional")", and he only aimed to create a sense of fiction through the film's aesthetics, drawing inspiration from both Chinese and Western stage plays.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 289  The screenplay emphasises Qiu Fu's status as a _chou_, which Qiu Jiongjiong referred to as the "clown spirit", calling it the "core and quintessence of his cinematic grammar".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) He cited [Federico Fellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Fellini "Federico Fellini")'s works as an inspiration, highlighting how [circus clowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circus_clown "Circus clown") served as [viewpoint characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viewpoint_character "Viewpoint character") in his films.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 288  In Sichuan opera, _chou_ roles (clowns) are usually not essential to the storyline but serve as the focal point, which Qiu referred to as the "author's perspective".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) In addition to Qiu Fu, Qiu Jiongjiong also created other clown-like characters, such as Crooky and Chicken Foot.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) These characters exist beyond the chronological timeline and the boundaries of the living and the dead in the plot, allowing them to serve as [narrators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrator "Narrator") and [storytellers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storytelling "Storytelling").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) He utilised these characters to interject the narrative to create a [distancing effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distancing_effect "Distancing effect"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-14) but rather than directly [breaking the fourth wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking_the_fourth_wall "Breaking the fourth wall"), Qiu aimed to re-examine the story naturally from the narrator and storyteller's perspectives.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)

Qiu drew inspiration from his personal experiences and [Sichuanese culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuanese_culture "Sichuanese culture") for the portrayal of clowns, noting that [Sichuanese people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuanese_people "Sichuanese people") are known for their optimism and [dark sense of humour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_humor "Dark humor") despite facing fate and suffering, qualities he found resonant with clowns' modest demeanor and playful exterior.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) Qiu also referenced the [Great Chinese Famine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Chinese_Famine "Great Chinese Famine") in the film, a topic often omitted in other [epic films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_film "Epic film") like _[Farewell My Concubine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell\_My\_Concubine\_(film) "Farewell My Concubine (film)")_ and _[The Blue Kite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blue\_Kite "The Blue Kite")_ (both 1993), explaining that he included it because he based the story primarily on his grandfather's biography and aimed to restore the original narrative.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) However, he noted that there are limited records about his grandfather's life during the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution"), and he had interviewed an elderly person knowledgeable about his grandfather's adoption of an infant girl for additional information.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) He concluded the screenplay with an [anticlimax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anticlimax_(narrative) "Anticlimax (narrative)") to reflect the daily lives of ordinary people, noting that while their stories may lack a [climactic arc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_arc "Character arc"), they can still convey profound emotional depth.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 296  The project was showcased at the [Golden Horse Project Promotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Horse_Film_Festival_and_Awards "Golden Horse Film Festival and Awards") in November 2017, where it won the CNC Prize from the [Centre national du cinéma et de l'image animée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre_national_du_cin%C3%A9ma_et_de_l%27image_anim%C3%A9e "Centre national du cinéma et de l'image animée").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-15) In May 2018, it received the Hubert Bals Fund at the [International Film Festival Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Film_Festival_Rotterdam "International Film Festival Rotterdam"), under the [working title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_title "Working title")_The Neo-New Adventures_,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-17)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-18) named after the opera troupe established at the film's opening.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) The first [table-read](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Table-read "Table-read") took place in the same month, and the cast was given a year to prepare for their characters.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia008-19)

Most of the actors and crew members are Qiu's family and friends, with many crew members also appeared in minor roles in the film.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) He cast them because he wanted to tell the story "locally", and described the shoot as a "party" among his closed ones.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Yi Sicheng, a film festival curator who befriended Qiu at the YunFest Film Festival and made a brief appearance in _Mr. Zhang Believes_, was invited by Qiu to star in the lead role.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia008-19) Qiu chose to avoid casting an actor of a similar age to the character Qiu Fu, as he felt the demeanor of actors around the same age as the character was unsuitable, and he was drawn to Yi's "old-timer" vibes, which he described as both "elegant and resilient".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia008-19) Guan Nan (who portrayed Tong Huafeng) and Xue Xuchan (who played dual roles as Hei and Chicken Foot) were also both film festival curators.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) Qiu chose Xue for the role of Chicken Foot due to his comedic awareness, and Xue received dialect coaching to prepare for his characters, as Hei speaks in [Southwestern Mandarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_Mandarin "Southwestern Mandarin") while Chicken Foot uses the [Leshan dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leshan_dialect "Leshan dialect") with an [Emei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeishan_City "Emeishan City") accent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) Qu Tao, an independent documentary filmmaker, was cast as the [aphasic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aphasia "Aphasia") character Crooky, specifically designed by Qiu because he believed Qu would struggle to remember the character's lines.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) Qiu Zhimin and Chen Haoyu, who played Pocky and young Qiu Fu, are Qiu Jiongjiong's father and nephew, respectively.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Despite initially hesitating to cast his father due to his age, Qiu Jiongjiong ultimately agreed when his father volunteered for the role, noting his similarities to Pocky.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-InitiumMediaApril2023-20) Qiu's cousin composed the film's score,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) drawing on elements from Sichuan opera,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) while his uncle served as the artistic advisor.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Qiu Jiongjiong made a cameo appearance at the end of the film, citing his reasons as being both the author and part of the [family history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_history "Family history") central to the story, as well as his desire to become part of the history of clowns as both a descendant and an enthusiast.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 294  All actors, except for the troupe teachers, were untrained, while the troupe roles were filled by professional Sichuan opera actors.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)

[![Image 2: Passengers in a small boat on the water, the scene is shrouded in mist](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/ed/ANewOldPlayBoatScene.png/250px-ANewOldPlayBoatScene.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ANewOldPlayBoatScene.png)

The film utilised visibly fake backdrops and set design, such as white fabrics to mimic turbulent waves during the disbandment scene of the New-New Theatre School, a style reminiscent of stage plays

Set construction spanned about six months.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) The shoot took place entirely at a factory owned by a friend of Qiu's, with the production set constructed in a [textile mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textile_mill "Textile mill") covering approximately 400 square meters (~4,306 square feet).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) A white shed was also built in the factory's parking lot, bringing the total size of the sets to about 1,000 square meters (~10,764 square feet).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) It was also the filming location for Qiu's previous film _Mr. Zhang Believes_, for which he wrote the screenplay with that set in mind.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 293  He likened the production style to the works of [Italo Calvino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italo_Calvino "Italo Calvino"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia006-21) and explained that he chose a similar set design with _Mr. Zhang Believes_ because he saw handcrafted production design as "an extension of creative invention", aiming to "refurbish through techniques" from early screen and stage plays.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Qiu Jiongjiong (who was a trained visual artist) served as the art director and participated in creating the set props.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia006-21)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) The set was mainly decorated with hand-painted artwork,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) while all the props, walls, staircases, and backdrops were also hand-crafted.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Most materials used for the set renovations were sourced directly from the surrounding factory, primarily utilising cloth, along with cardboard, wood, and cotton.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3)

Qiu emphasised that he chose to use "exaggerated" set and props to suit the film's tone of absurdity and [black humour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_humour "Black humour").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 289  He also created and manipulated a "sense of alienation" through low-budget filmmaking, using visibly fake backgrounds and a theatrical style of production sets, influenced by [Bertolt Brecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertolt_Brecht "Bertolt Brecht")'s plays.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) For instance, a grey cloth was used to represent a river,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) while wind-blown plastic bags and shaking white fabrics were used to mimic the turbulent waves,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-34SMFebruary2023-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-LianheZaobaoReview-23) with critics comparing the scantily decorated settings to [Roy Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Andersson "Roy Andersson")'s films.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ChinaFilmNewsReview-24) Lin Sheng-wei at _[United Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United\_Daily\_News "United Daily News")_ compared the "flimsy" and simplistic scenery to [stage plays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stage_play "Stage play"), calling it a "forced [defamiliarization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defamiliarization "Defamiliarization")" that required the audience to "use their imagination in every scene", which encourages the audience to focus on the characters and immerse in their emotions to "make the absurd props come to life";[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-25) while _[34th Street Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/34th\_Street\_Magazine "34th Street Magazine")_'s Weike Li described the "obviously contrived sets" as "intentionally creating a sense of comical foreignness", presenting history in [expressionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expressionism "Expressionism").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-34SMFebruary2023-22) While designing the [netherworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youdu "Youdu"), Qiu cited [Jacques Tati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Tati "Jacques Tati")'s visual style as an inspiration, and made limited distinctions from the living world sets, primarily by dimming the [lighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_lighting "Film lighting") and using black-coloured props instead of white.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-InitiumMediaApril2023-20)

[![Image 3: Arched red bridge with pagoda-like structures spanning a river against a backdrop of lush greenery](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/Leshan_%2816989556077%29.jpg/250px-Leshan_%2816989556077%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Leshan_(16989556077).jpg)

Filming took place at Qiu Jiongjiong's hometown [Leshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leshan "Leshan")

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began in August 2019 in Leshan, Sichuan, China,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia008-19)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesTing-26) the hometown of Qiu Jiongjiong.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) Filming lasted a total of 83 days over a three-month period.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Robbin Feng served as the cinematographer,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-27) using an [Arri Alexa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arri_Alexa "Arri Alexa") for the shoot, a camera model that Qiu described as "better than anything [he had] worked with before".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) In terms of cinematography, [horizontal shifts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracking_shot "Tracking shot") and [lateral camera movements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panning_(camera) "Panning (camera)") were primarily employed to present the composition as an "unveiling scroll of [Chinese painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_painting "Chinese painting")".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia006-21) The composition was mainly planimetric, with the camera positioned at a 90-degree angle to the actors and utilising perpendicular [tracking shots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracking_shot "Tracking shot").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) Qiu aimed to convey a sense of [epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_poetry "Epic poetry") scale by emphasising the shallow depth of field in the set design,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia006-21) and compared the composition to the [triptychs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triptych "Triptych") and [frescoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frescoes "Frescoes") of [Giotto di Bondone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giotto_di_Bondone "Giotto di Bondone").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) The production team planned the shooting schedule in advance, allowing set pieces to be disassembled and reassembled between scenes.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) The costumes used in the film were all from Qiu Jiongjiong's father's former opera troupe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4)

The entire cast stayed in Leshan for a month after filming to record their dialogues,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) as no sounds were [recorded on location](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound_recording_and_reproduction "Sound recording and reproduction") during filming.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-MirrorMedia006-21)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) Qiu cited several reasons for this decision, including to avoid the high costs of on-site recording, the background noises at the factory, and the fact that most of the actors were non-locals who could not speak in standard Leshan dialects, therefore he decided to record dialogue after the filming wrapped.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) He also noted that it could enable the dialects to be delivered more precisely, allowing actors to adjust their emotions for a better performance, while [crowd scenes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowd_scene "Crowd scene") and scenes without visible lip movements also permit changes to the dialogue.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) He chose to feature the film's dialogues in [Sichuanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuanese_dialects "Sichuanese dialects"), his native language, which he described as "vivid and humorous" and having a "strong nostalgia" stemming from the dialect's evolution over hundreds of years since [the diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuanese_people "Sichuanese people") from other [provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_China "Provinces of China") during the [Ming Dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_Dynasty "Ming Dynasty").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) This film is the second to be made primarily in Sichuanese since _Conscription_ (1962).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)[Dubbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubbing "Dubbing") was supervised by [sound designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound_designer "Sound designer") Wang Ran, who also created all the sound effects for the film.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4)

### Portrayal of history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=A_New_Old_Play&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Portrayal of history")]

_A New Old Play_ chronicles a series of [Chinese historical events from the 1920s to the 1980s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_China#Modern_China "History of China"), including the collapse of the [Qing dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_dynasty "Qing dynasty"), the [Warlord Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warlord_Era "Warlord Era"), [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and the [fall of Nanking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanjing_Massacre "Nanjing Massacre"), the [Chinese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War "Chinese Civil War"), [Mao Zedong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong")'s [Communist Party rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party"), the [Great Chinese Famine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Chinese_Famine "Great Chinese Famine"), the [Great Leap Forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Leap_Forward "Great Leap Forward"), and the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-33) Qiu Jiongjiong identified a theme of the film as the notion that history endlessly repeats itself.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6) He summarised that the film's overall tone conveys the tragedy of destiny, aiming to create a contrast between the vividness of each individual and the cruelty of their irresistible fates.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 292  Qiu also explained that he found many historical narratives focus on context or abstract ideologies, but when the emphasis is placed on particular individuals, it becomes easier to "identify certain problems".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-34)

Film scholar [Hao Jian](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hao_Jian&action=edit&redlink=1 "Hao Jian (page does not exist)")([zh](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%83%9D%E5%BB%BA "zh:郝建")) specifically commented on the film's approach to presenting [historical memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_memory "Historical memory") through familial and personal experiences, which aligns with [Michel Foucault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Foucault "Michel Foucault")'s discourse on popular memory and allows for a "faithful" portrayal of history, but from a new perspective that reinterprets and questions history—specifically, in the case of _A New Old Play_, from the perspective of a clown and infused with a sense of comedy.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-JianMay2024-35): 145–146  Qiu stated that he did not intend to recreate historical scenes but rather aimed to convey a general sense of the historical context of that time through metaphorical expressions, such as the film's simplistic and theatrical production style.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4) Academic Isha Ting noted that the film's aesthetics resonate with Brecht's distancing effect, which encourages the audience to focus on social roots and structures while reflecting on what can be transformed.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesTing-26)

> "In this film, the connection between those onstage and offstage, as well as inside and outside the Sichuan opera being put together in the story, is blurred. What happens onstage is integrated into the narrative, and the expressions onstage are blended into the characters' everyday lives. This is because Sichuan opera took root in my body and soul through the mundanity of everyday life. Just like when generations of Sichuan opera goers, who spent much of their time in the theater weeping, sighing, falling asleep, etc., their lives are in a way inter-textualized with the performance on stage, creating an adventitious symmetry of life itself; were they just watching a performance, or are they themselves a part of, or even integrated into the performance?"

—Qiu Jiongjiong on incorporating the characteristics of Sichuan opera into the narrative[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9)

Qiu described his motive for creating _A New Old Play_ as a desire to craft a "Sichuan-flavored saga", incorporating local elements without reducing them to conceptualised spectacles or [stereotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereotype "Stereotype").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Notable elements added to the film include [Sichuanese people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuanese_people "Sichuanese people"), [Sichuan opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan_opera "Sichuan opera"), and [Sichuanese dialects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuanese_dialects "Sichuanese dialects"), all heavily influenced by the culture surrounding him during his upbringing.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BeijingYouthDailyJanuary2023-36)

Regarding Sichuan opera, Qiu sought to transform the traditional operatic language into a more accessible form of expression that could effectively communicate while retaining its flavor and melodies, sharing similarities with the works of [Geoffrey Chaucer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Chaucer "Geoffrey Chaucer"), [François Rabelais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Rabelais "François Rabelais"), and [Giovanni Boccaccio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Boccaccio "Giovanni Boccaccio").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Despite featuring exaggerated theatrical staging in its production design, film scholar [Michael Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Berry_(scholar)&action=edit&redlink=1 "Michael Berry (scholar) (page does not exist)")([zh](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%99%BD%E7%9D%BF%E6%96%87 "zh:白睿文")) observed that these production values closely parallel Sichuan opera, which enhance the authenticity and emotional depth of the performances while maintaining the overall tone of [realism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Realism_(arts) "Realism (arts)").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 292  Qiu identified the characteristics of Sichuan opera as "mundanity of everyday life" filled with expressions of deep and personal humanity, and he integrated these characteristics into the story, blending the ordinary with the daily lives of the characters.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) He compared the viewing experience to that of opera-goers [inter-textualizing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intertextuality "Intertextuality") with the stage performances, creating a symmetry with their own lives and immersing themselves in the performance.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-DGenerateMarch2022-9) Scholar [Wong Nim-yan](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wong_Nim-yan&action=edit&redlink=1 "Wong Nim-yan (page does not exist)")([zh](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%BB%83%E5%BF%B5%E6%AC%A3 "zh:黃念欣")) also recognised this perspective, noting that there are limited Sichuan opera scenes in the film, but the cinematography, production design, and dialogues strongly resemble it, and compared its central thought to traditional Sichuan opera pieces like _Inn of Successive Promotion_ (連升店) and _Writing Essays_ (做文章), suggesting that the film itself can be viewed as a form of Sichuan opera.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-37)

The film also explores [thanatology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanatology "Thanatology"), which Qiu describes as stemming from the Sichuanese people's understanding of life and death.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 294  A significant part of the film is set in the [underworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underworld "Underworld"), using a secular perspective to speculate about the [afterlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afterlife "Afterlife").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 294  He found that the Sichuanese people hold an optimistic view of death, citing traditional _Ba Ba banquets_ (壩壩宴), family banquets held for both weddings and funerals, as an example and describing them as a reflection of the Sichuanese perspective on death as "a harmony between sorrow and joy".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BeijingYouthDailyJanuary2023-36) He composed the story in which the protagonist reflects on his life and anticipates his post-death journey, aligning it with Sichuanese views on death and describing the film as "a flowing banquet of life and death".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-BerryVoiceover-8): 294

_A New Old Play_, like all of Qiu Jiongjiong's previous documentaries, was unable to obtain a [film public screening permit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_public_screening_permit "Film public screening permit") from the [China Film Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Film_Administration "China Film Administration"), which prevented its official release in China and only unauthorised private screenings were held in the country from 2021 to 2022.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesTing-26) Une Cinema De Vent, the non-profit organisation managing these private screenings, stated that the production team wanted to avoid [self-censorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-censorship "Self-censorship") regarding content and therefore adopted an approach to screen the film globally by contacting various distributors to host single-time private screenings.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-PArticlesMarch2023-3) Filmmaker [Geling Yan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geling_Yan "Geling Yan"), while discussing [film censorship in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_censorship_in_China "Film censorship in China"), cited _A New Old Play_ as an example of the growing discontent among filmmakers regarding censorship, and referred to its unauthorised screenings as an alternative approach to filmmaking, distinct from simply shifting production outside the country.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-58)

_A New Old Play_'s critical reception was positive,[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-59) with _[Liberty Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty\_Times "Liberty Times")_ referring to it as "critically acclaimed".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-60) On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), [100%](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_with_a_100%25_rating_on_Rotten_Tomatoes "List of films with a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes") of 9 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 8.5/10.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-61) As of August 2022, the film held a rating of 9.0/10 on the Chinese media review platform [Douban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douban "Douban"),[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-62) for which the _[International Examiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International\_Examiner "International Examiner")_ described the score as "well received".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-InternationalExaminerSeptember2022-51)

Austin Considine of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ described _A New Old Play_ as a "magnificently layered historical epic", blending tragedy and farce with crafted [mise-en-scène](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mise-en-sc%C3%A8ne "Mise-en-scène"), while infusing humour into a narrative that grapples with the "absurdities and indignities" of life amidst the turmoil of Chinese history.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-NYTReview-1)_[Film Threat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film\_Threat "Film Threat")_'s Calan Panchoo rated the film 8.5/10, praising its "astonishing imagination" in combining art and history through a "salient" presentation achieved with "beautifully realized" production design, "wickedly puckish humor", and a "wonderful visual suggestion" that balances [realism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Realism_(arts) "Realism (arts)") and [surrealism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrealism "Surrealism"), resulting in a "multilayered" exploration of history and memory in contemporary Chinese history.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-FilmThreatReview-63)

[Richard Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Brody "Richard Brody") at _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ found the story to be a "daringly and imaginatively" dramatised account of 20th-century Chinese political history, presenting a highly personal and intimate portrayal of a small theatre company amid ongoing [film censorship in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_censorship_in_China "Film censorship in China"), employing theatrical techniques and "archly" ironic elements to emphasise the narrative's complexities.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-NewYorkerReview-2) Marta Bałaga, writing for _[Cineuropa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cineuropa "Cineuropa")_, called the film an "extraordinary" epic saga that, despite its "demanding" narrative richness and complex themes, remains a "pleasure, frequently humorous and always tender" exploration of the Sichuan opera performers' lives amidst China's political turmoil, showcasing director Qiu Jiongjiong's deep affection for the art form.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-64) Stéphane Gobbo of _[Le Temps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Temps "Le Temps")_ also acknowledged the film's "wonderful homage" to traditional Chinese theatre and early cinema through its production design, noting that it effectively addresses historical themes with a unique and immersive narrative style.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-65)

_[InReview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InReview "InReview")_'s Ryan Swen regarded the film as a "rich and complex contribution to the Chinese folk tradition", comparing it to _[The Travelling Players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Travelling\_Players "The Travelling Players")_ (1975) and _[Platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platform\_(2000\_film) "Platform (2000 film)")_ (2000) for their shared use of theatrical performances to depict history, while lauding its bold blend of theatricality and stylisation that creates an "intimate and aggregative" portrait of a [clown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chou_role "Chou role")'s journey through 20th-century history, ultimately celebrating the artistry of theatre amidst the inevitability of historical change and uncertainties.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-66) Wang Xia, on the other hand, noted similarities between the film and the works of [Roy Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Andersson "Roy Andersson") in her review for _[China Film News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China\_Film\_News "China Film News")_, commending the "decent" and surrealistic production designs that connect to paintings, poetry, and theatre, while acknowledging the use of traditional theatrical performance's fictional elements to explore over half a century of Chinese history, "ingeniously balancing the absurd and the profound" in its reflection on themes of dignity, humour, and the interconnectedness of life and death.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ChinaFilmNewsReview-24)

1.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_ref-5 "Jump up")**The Chicken foot god (Chinese: 雞腳神) is a [gnome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gnome "Gnome")-like creature in Sichuanese mythology.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-ThePaperJanuary2023-4)
2.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_ref-10 "Jump up")**_Chou_ role (丑角) is literally translated as "[clown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clown "Clown") role" in English, although _xiaochou_ (小丑), the Chinese term for clown, carries different connotations compared to _chou_ role in Sichuan opera.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6)
3.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_ref-18 "Jump up")**In an interview with _[Cinema Scope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema\_Scope "Cinema Scope")_, Qiu Jiongjiong referred to the working title as _The Adventures of the New-New Theatre_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6)
4.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_ref-32 "Jump up")**_Jiaoma_ (椒麻) refers to the spicy bite of [Sichuan pepper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan_pepper "Sichuan pepper"), a common flavor in [Sichuan cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan_cuisine "Sichuan cuisine"), while _tanghui_ (堂會) refers to private banquets hosted by the wealthy, such as weddings or funerals, featuring entertainers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Old_Play#cite_note-CinemaScopeSeptember2022-6)

A New Old Play
==============

椒麻堂会
----

### QIU Jiongjiong

179 minutes | 2021 | Fiction | Sichuanese Dialect| English Subtitles

**Canadian Premiere**

**7 PM, SAT, AUG 20

 Innis Town Hall**Closing Night Screening

GET TICKETS

One evening in the 1980s, Qiu Fu, a leading clown-role actor in 20th-century Sichuan opera, departs this world and must reluctantly set off for the Ghost City under the escort of two underworld officials. Along the way, he meets old friends. As they recall the past, earthly scenes creep into the mists of the Netherworld.

Qiu Fu’s life in opera unfolds against the backdrop of a secular upheaval. The “New-New” Troupe in which he grows up and learns his trade is affiliated with the military. As power shifts, the troupe is cast loose to wander rootlessly through a broken world. Despite this unsettled destiny, shaped by war, famine and political turmoil, Qiu Fu becomes one of the finest clown-role performers in Sichuan opera. And yet, one day he finds himself clapped in a pigsty as a political revolution rages outside.

Outside the Ghost City, sitting among familiar faces, Qiu Fu drinks the mandatory bowl of Forgetfulness Soup to erase his memory. A lifetime of hardship, pain and sorrow, all vanish as if they had never been.

Director
--------

![Image 5: A man sitting on a chair and holding a cigarette in his right hand](https://mulanfestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/copy-of-a-new-old-play-04_director-jiongjiong-qiu-scaled-300x225.jpeg)QIU Jiongjiong (born 1977) is an active contemporary artist and filmmaker in China. His work as an artist has been exhibited worldwide. As a filmmaker, his experiments with cinematic language and aesthetics in documentary film-making have earned him a reputation as one of China’s most important independent directors. His experimental/documentary feature _Mr. Zhang Believes_ (2015), premiered at the Locarno International Film Festival and has been screened internationally. _Jiao Ma Tang Hui_(_A New Old Play_) is his first fiction feature.

QIU Jiongjiong’s visually magnificent new film is a unique hybrid of fiction, historical reminiscence, and experimental theatre. Its overview of China from the 1930s to the 1980s is filtered through Qiu Yu, a Sichuan opera 'clown' based on the director’s own famous grandfather. As Qiu Yu negotiates his entry into Hades with two comic sidekicks, his departing soul reviews his childhood, his performances, family tragedies, and political perils.

This film of unparalleled aesthetic and political courage takes place in modestly spectacular visual settings: Qiu, a famous artist, has handcrafted an exquisite miniature model village, a fantastical river landscape, a golden sun in the shape of a Buddha’s head. These images set the scene for a constantly shifting acting style that embraces absurdism, political melodrama, comic vaudeville, and ritual tableaux. We are offered memory as a re-lived collective experience, insistently comic in its mode, but expansively humane in its vision. —IFFR

After the war, when the adult Qiu Fu (Yi Sicheng) emerges as a star, the theatre faces pressure from the Communist Party; in the sixties, the Cultural Revolution proves catastrophic. Qiu Jiongjiong tells this story with affecting intimacy and candid observation—and with archly ironic methods. The movie is filmed as theatrical tableaux, complete with blatantly contrived sets and supernatural fantasy sequences, which virtually shout at viewers not to take the depicted events as literal truth._(May 13.)_ Published in the print edition of the [May 23, 2022](https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2022/05/23), issue. [### Wes Anderson China-Style](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt14864160/reviews/?featured=rw9188146&ref_=tt_ururv_c_1_hd)

Mythologies about the afterlife can get somewhat confusing. Some simply believe that you die and you either go "up" or "down," to heaven or to hell. Still others believe there is a sort of waiting room, a purgatory, or a place where you just take a number and wait your turn (like in Beetlejuice). I recommend the hilarious "Defending Your Life," an Albert Brooks film that explores the process in Judgment City whereby ones' future placement is determined.

In China, Nieh-ching-t'ai is a place in the Underworld where souls must review their lives before a mirror until the Yama King makes his judgment. And that is precisely the context for this film, which at its open finds the famous actor Qiu Fu (Yi Sicheng) entering the Underworld. He is greeted by two demons, Oxhead and Horseface aka Oxey and Horsey from Fengdu, the capital of Hell. They will be accompanying him on his journey through the Nieh-ching-t'ai.

Beginning in 1920, when Qui was just a child starting his training with the New-New Theatrical Troupe, the film takes us through Qui's life and experience in a series of tableaus depicting the characters and experiences of the day. The movie reminded me of a Wes Anderson film in style. Along the way 20th century Chinese history is explored, along with some commentary on that history.

My Wes Anderson comment is as much about the humor as it is the visual style. Comedy abounds in A New Old Play. The film is beautifully composed and cinematographically gorgeous. This is a masterpiece of Chinese independent cinema that may make its way onto some critics must see lists in years to come. The director Qiu Jiongjiong, who found inspiration from his own grandfather who was an actor like the Qui in the film, said, "I have rejected any tedious speculation, or supercilious detachment, in favor of lively, unabashed good humor and fun. . . The Dionysian spirit, the vital force, the clown in each of us. . . Hovering between reality and fantasy." It was a pleasure watching all 180 minutes of A New Old Play, released by Kani, and available at Vinegar Syndrome.
